findings.F1: The test's measure is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: across 286 independent signal events the mean excess 5-day return is -0.0089 with t = -1.51, only 52% of events negative, and the median-split check passes at -0.0086.
findings.F2: The effect is graded as the idea says but carried by the strongest cases. The third with the most negative forecasts has a mean excess 5-day return of -0.0190 (t = -2.01, n = 95), the middle third -0.0114 (t = -0.95), and the weakest third +0.0034 (t = +0.37).

ideas.name: heavy-volume drop, more coins
ideas.idea: When a coin falls sharply over one day on volume well above its own 30-day average daily volume, it keeps falling over the next 5 days. The larger the fall and the heavier its volume against that average, the larger the further loss.
ideas.consequence: A sharp drop on heavy volume reflects many traders acting on new information that is still spreading, so the decline carries on as slower traders arrive.

ideas.idea: When a coin falls sharply over one day on volume well above its own 30-day average daily volume, it keeps falling over the next 5 days, only for the largest falls on the heaviest volume against that average. The larger the fall and the heavier its volume against that average, the larger the further loss.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts, or refuses to buy the dip, only after the largest one-day falls on the heaviest volume, and expects the loss to show over the following week rather than the next day.
ideas.name: strongest heavy-volume drops continue
